`agentHost.skillInvoked` records what triggered each SDK `skill.invoked`, for the main agent and mapped subagents. A subagent the host cannot map is dropped like its other events and remains only on `copilotSdk/skill_invoked`. The trigger is `agent-invoked`, `user-invoked` or `context-load`, and anything else becomes `unknown`. The event also records where the skill came from. `skillSource` is the runtime's discovery source (`project`, `inherited`, `personal-copilot`, `personal-agents`, `custom`, `plugin`, `builtin`, `remote`, `sdk`, `mcp`, else `other` or `unknown`). `skillOrigin` says who shipped it: `vscode` (served by the host's skill provider: `troubleshoot` and `model-router`), `runtime` (the runtime's `builtin` skills and skills in its bundled plugin directories), or `other`. Skills from workspace, personal or organization sources (`project`, `inherited`, `personal-*`, `remote`) are always `other`, even under a runtime plugin directory. Skills VS Code syncs to the runtime, such as Agents window and extension skills, are also `other`: they reach the runtime as copies under user data, mixed with third-party skills, so their location does not prove who shipped them. `skillName` is the plain name only when `skillOrigin` is `vscode` or `runtime`; no other skill is named, because a user's skill name can identify them, even when it matches a built-in name. Join it to the forwarded `copilotSdk/skill_invoked` on `sdkEventId` = `event_id` to get the hashed skill and plugin names of other skills. A subagent invocation is reported against the subagent chat, the root turn it was invoked in (nested subagents inherit it from their spawning subagent), and the account captured when it started. It never takes these from whatever turn is current, because a background subagent can outlive or straddle root turns. A slash command naming a plugin skill by its bare name (`/commit` for `VS Code Synced Data:commit`) resolves to that skill when the name is unambiguous. It then runs through `commands.invoke` and reports `user-invoked`, rather than reaching the model as plain text and reporting `agent-invoked`. The model can load the same skill again within that turn (`agent-invoked`), so to count only skills the agent chose on its own, exclude agent rows whose turn has a user row for the same skill.

+`agentHost.toolInvoked` and the agent host's `languageModelToolInvoked` report who provides each tool in `toolSourceKind`: `agentHost`, `mcp`, `client`, or `unknown`. A call to a tool the session does not offer, usually a name the model invented, reports `unknown` with `errorCode` `toolNotFound`, so it is not counted as a built-in tool that failed. Its `toolId` is a `sha256:` hash of the requested name, because the name is arbitrary model output. The tracker keys only on the tool call's `error.code` `toolNotFound`. The Copilot provider sets that code (in `getSdkToolCallError`, live and on restore) when the runtime's tool telemetry has `failure_reason` `not_found`, because the runtime's own `error.code` is the generic `failure`. A runtime that stops reporting that reason leaves these calls as built-in failures.

Four events from `node/copilot/copilotComputerUseTelemetry.ts` track Computer Use. They carry only categories, counts and durations, never app names, window titles or typed text. Tool calls are in `agentHost.toolInvoked`, with a `toolId` that starts with `computer-use-` and `mcpSourceKind` `builtin`.
